publicationStatus: Unpublished; three proposed articles remain status review. Independent editorial review and maintainer adoption are pending; no merge or deployment has occurred.
method: Reopened claim-bearing public primary/official sources for T323, T041 and T341. Historical object statements are separated from NICENESS design descriptions. No original research photos, scan identifiers, full official product copy, or third-party images were added. T041 does not identify a specific Leonardo drawing. T341 leaves the relationship between the product-page country label and sewing attribution unresolved and does not claim finished-garment origin. All three drafts remain review-only. Hash equality identifies research snapshots; it does not replace independent editorial review or maintainer adoption.

usedFacts.claim: NPS records a circa-1950 single-breasted western-style sports jacket combining leather and tan herringbone, made by California Sportswear Co. in Los Angeles.
NICENESS’s user-attested official archive describes H.KENT as drawing on 1950s–60s US sports jackets and UK hunting jackets, then using reversible double-woven worsted construction with fewer seams.

sources.title: Sports Jacket - Circa 1950
sources.publisher: Harry S Truman National Historic Site

sourceChecks.verifiedClaim: The live NPS entry identifies the garment as single-breasted, leather and tan herringbone, western style, circa 1950, made by California Sportswear Co., Los Angeles.
Used only as a separately attributed NICENESS design statement; the archive source does not identify the NPS jacket as H.KENT’s direct reference.

records.claimsStatus: The NPS entry confirms one garment’s label and construction. It does not identify a wearer or sporting use. H.KENT’s official archive refers to broader categories and does not name this NPS item.
records.boundary: The historical object and NICENESS statement are separate. No claim is made that the NPS jacket was worn by Truman or directly inspired H.KENT.

usedFacts.claim: NICENESS’s GUARINO page attributes the body to a 1970s British casual shirt, sleeve/collar details to French dress-shirt patterns, the dobby fabric to an Italian mill operating since the 1950s, and detail finishing to hand sewing.

sourceChecks.verifiedClaim: The live page states the design references and hand-sewn detail finish; it displays MADE IN JAPAN while the description also attributes sewing to Salvatore Piccolo in Italy, without explaining their relationship.

records.claimsStatus: The product page supports a design statement and hand-finish claim. It does not name the specific hand-sewn seams. Its country label and sewing attribution are not reconciled, so final-garment origin is left unasserted.
records.boundary: The article separates inspiration/material geography from finished-garment origin. It makes no country-of-manufacture claim and does not infer which stitches were hand-sewn.
